The '''2025 New Zealand Men's National League''' (known as the '''[[Dettol]] Men's National League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the fifth scheduled season of the [[New Zealand National League|National League]] since its restructuring in 2021; the [[2021 New Zealand National League|2021]] National League was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand|COVID-19 pandemic]] in northern regions.<ref name="NZF-021121">{{cite web |title=National League Championship cancelled, new interregional competition announced and Chatham Cup moved to 2022 |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/109383 |website=New Zealand Football}}</ref> 32 clubs compete in the competition, with four qualifying from the [[Northern League (New Zealand)|Northern League]], three qualifying from the [[Central League (New Zealand)|Central League]] and two qualifying from the [[Southern League (New Zealand)|Southern League]] for the National Championship phase.<ref name="phxchamps"/><ref name="NLSystem">{{cite web |title=New National League system |url=https://www.sporty.co.nz/asset/downloadasset?id=3da9f0fa-187f-406d-8e40-e5a936662fcc |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=3 April 2021}}</ref> Auckland FC Reserves and Wellington Phoenix Reserves qualify automatically for the championship phase.
Each team can field a maximum of four foreign players as well as one additional foreign player who has [[Oceania Football Confederation]] nationality.<ref name="breach">{{cite web |title=Two National League clubs found to have breached foreign player regulations |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/102667 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=23 April 2021 |archive-date=23 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210423021812/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/102667 |url-status=dead }}</ref> 
Over the course of the season, each team must also ensure players aged 20 or under account for 10% of available playing minutes.<ref name="under20s">{{cite web |title=National League regulations for U-20 players revised |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/121766 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=9 March 2023 }}</ref>

The qualifying league fixtures were announced on 28 February 2025. The Northern League started on 15 March 2025 with the Central and Southern leagues starting on the 29 March. The Northern and Central leagues concluded on 30 August 2025 with the Southern League concluding on 31 August 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/150711|title=Fixtures Announced for the Dettol National League 2025, with Auckland FC Joining the Men’s Competition for the First Time|website=New Zealand Football|date=28 February 2025|access-date=28 February 2025}}</ref>

The 2025 Northern League is the 60th season, 5th season since the restructure of the leagues, of premiership football in the Upper [[North Island]]. The League started on 15 March and finishes on 30 August, with the top four side qualifying for the [[#Championship phase|National League Championship]] along with the already qualified [[Auckland FC Reserves]].
====Northern League teams====
Twelve teams are competing in the league – the top ten teams from the previous season, one team promoted from the [[2024 NRFL Leagues#Championship|NRFL Championship]] and [[Auckland FC Reserves]]. The promoted team is [[Fencibles United]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2024/08/25/fencibles-united-clinch-championship-title-and-promotion-to-northern-league/|title=Fencibles United clinch Championship title and promotion to Northern League|website=friendsoffootballnz.com|access-date=7 December 2024|date=25 August 2024}}</ref> It is both Auckland FC Reserves's and Fencibles United's first season in the National League. They replaced [[Melville United AFC|Melville United]] and [[Hamilton Wanderers AFC|Hamilton Wanderers]] (both relegated after a four-year Northern League spell).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.waibopfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/149109?newsfeedId=551387|title=Promotion and Relegation: NRFL and WaiBOP Leagues|website=WaiBOP Football|access-date=2 February 2025|date=15 January 2025}}</ref>

The 2025 Central League is the 29th season, 5th season since the restructure of the leagues, of premiership football in the Lower [[North Island]]. The League starts on 29 March and finishes on 30 August, with the top three side qualifying for the [[#Championship phase|National League Championship]] along with the already qualified [[Wellington Phoenix FC Reserves|Wellington Phoenix Reserves]].
==== Central League teams ====
Ten teams are competing in the league – the top nine teams from the previous season and the one team promoted from the 2024 play-off between the winners of the [[Central Federation League]] and the [[Capital Premier (New Zealand)|Capital Premier]]. The winner of the play-off was [[Upper Hutt City FC|Upper Hutt City]].<ref>{{cite web |date=14 September 2024 |title=Day of reckoning settles Central League participation for next season |url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2024/09/14/day-of-reckoning-settles-central-league-participation-for-next-season/ |website=friendsoffootballnz.com |access-date=7 December 2024}}</ref> This is their first season in the Central League, since New Zealand football's restructuring in 2021. They replaced [[Stop Out Sports Club|Stop Out]] (relegated to the Central Federation League after two seasons in the Central League).<ref>{{cite web |date=29 November 2024 |title=James Sutcliffe to lead Stop Out in next season's Central League 2 |url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2024/11/29/james-sutcliffe-to-lead-stop-out-in-next-seasons-central-league-2/ |website=friendsoffootballnz.com |access-date=7 December 2024}}</ref>

The 2025 Southern League is the 4th season of a full 10 team league, 5th season since the restructure of the leagues, of a [[South Island]] wide football league. The League started on 29 March and finished on 13 September, with the top two side qualifying for the [[#Championship phase|National League Championship]].

==== Southern League teams ====
Ten teams are competing in the league – the top nine teams from the previous season and the winner of the Southern League play-offs. The promoted team is [[Wanaka AFC|Wānaka]].<ref>{{cite web |date=6 October 2024 |title=Wanaka clinch promotion to Southern League after winning play-off series |url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2024/10/06/wanaka-clinch-promotion-to-southern-league-after-winning-play-off-series/ |website=friendsoffootballnz.com |access-date=5 December 2024}}</ref> This is their first season in the Southern League. They replaced [[FC Twenty 11]] (relegated to the [[Canterbury Premiership League]] after their second season in the Southern League).<ref>{{cite web |date=13 September 2024 |title=PREVIEW: Battle begins for promotion to next year’s Southern League |url=https://www.friendsoffootballnz.com/2024/09/13/preview-battle-begins-for-promotion-to-next-years-southern-league/ |website=friendsoffootballnz.com |access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref>

The table lists the positions of teams after each week of matches. To preserve chronological evolvements, any postponed matches are not included in the round at which they were originally scheduled, but added to the full round they were played immediately afterwards.
